extensions.description: The result envelope's extension map. Every block THIS kernel emits is declared in themis.blocks and has a sub-schema below — a test holds the two lists equal in both directions, because for a long time it held only one, and eight blocks carrying four hundred instances a run sat outside the schema with nobody able to say what domain their fields had. The map stays open all the same: `verify()` accepts an envelope carrying somebody else's annotation, and what closes our own emission is the registry check at the two exits, not this. Openness is for foreign blocks; it was never a licence for ours.

assumption_ledger.description: Everything the answer takes on faith, worst first — the block both the report and the browser lead with. One line carries three closed vocabularies and they are declared here because all three leave the kernel and are read by two independent surfaces: `layer` (which part of the answer stops being true), `severity` (how badly the conclusion dies), `provenance` (who put it on the list, and is therefore who the reader argues with). They had no enum and no table anywhere, which is how `layer` came to hold a sixth value named `assumption` on an assumption ledger, and how an empty string in either field passed the verifier. `severity` is the grade of `layer` and not a second fact about the assumption — a consumer may read it without knowing the mapping, but the kernel derives it from `layer` at one place and the verifier re-derives it, so the two can never disagree. `claim` is free prose and `id` is the flat declaration this entry is the structured form of, when it has one.

identification.description: Which pattern the graph was recognised as, beside the formula it produced. `pattern` is the one field with a closed vocabulary, and it is declared because a vocabulary that leaves the kernel has to be checkable by whoever states it to a reader — as the three sibling pattern-like fields (selection_recovery.criterion, missing_data_recovery.mechanism, mediation_decomposition.strategy) already are. The companions a pattern brings are declared too, and the map is closed. It used to stay open on the argument that their PRESENCE is what the pattern decides — which is true, and which is what an OPTIONAL property says. Declaring a field is not requiring it, so openness bought nothing for optionality while costing the one thing a closed map gives: that a misspelled writer key raises instead of vanishing. `joint_identification.pattern` is a DIFFERENT vocabulary (joint_backdoor / joint_general_id) on a different block.

adjustment_set.description: backdoor only: the set a reader is told to control for.

mediator_set.description: front_door only: the mediators the effect is routed through.

conditioned_on.description: Present when the estimand is conditional: the Z of P(Y | do(X), Z), which is part of the question rather than of the adjustment.

estimand.description: Present when the conditional estimand is the IDC ratio rather than a plain adjustment.

instrument.description: instrumental_variable only: the chosen instrument, copied from iv_identification because this block is the human surface.

conditioning.description: instrumental_variable only: the set within which the instrument is valid.

required_assumption.description: instrumental_variable only: the estimation-layer assumption point identification still needs.

selection_recovery.description: Phase 9 §S9.1: Bareinboim-Pearl recoverability from selection bias. Attached to an effect result whose sample is restricted (ObservationStatement) on a selection collider of X and Y — the constructive counterpart to the selection_on_collider_opens_path gap. Says whether the unbiased P(y|do(x)) is s-recoverable from the biased sample via the selection-backdoor criterion, with what recovery formula, and what external (unbiased) data (if any) is required. A recoverable=false verdict means 'not via selection-backdoor adjustment', not a proof of non-recoverability (the complete algorithm is out of scope).

adjustment_set.description: The full selection-backdoor adjustment set Z = Z⁺ ∪ Z⁻.

z_plus.description: Non-descendants of X within Z (control confounding, back-door part).

z_minus.description: Descendants of X within Z (control selection only; reweighted, not used for back-door blocking).

external_data_needed.description: Unbiased distributions required beyond the biased sample P(v|S); empty ⇒ recoverable from the biased data alone.

longitudinal_identification.description: Phase 7.L: g-formula / sequential-back-door identification of a time-varying treatment STRATEGY effect (Hernán & Robins ch.21). Attached to the effect result the program's options.longitudinal spec designates. identified=true means the strategy contrast E[Y_ā=treated] − E[Y_ā=control] is point-identified by the g-formula: at each time k the measured history H_k = {L_0..L_k, A_0..A_{k-1}} blocks every back-door path from A_k to Y (sequential exchangeability, an untestable premise the graph confirms is sufficient for the DECLARED measured history). identified=false means an unblocked back-door remains at some treatment — the g-formula would return a biased number, and the numeric layer refuses to ship one.

confounders_by_time.description: Covariate blocks measured before each treatment; index k holds L_k (after A_{k-1}, before A_k).

assumptions.description: The untestable identification premises (sequential exchangeability, positivity, consistency).

missing_data_recovery.description: Phase 9 §S9.2: Mohan-Pearl-Tian recoverability from missing data. Attached to an effect result when the program declares ≥1 missingness_indicator. Classifies the mechanism (MCAR/MAR/MNAR); the top-level keys describe the g-formula ADJUSTED CONDITIONAL P(Y | X, given, Z) — Z the back-door adjustment set — recovered from the missing data via an ordered factorization. The full interventional estimand P(Y | do(X)) = Σ_z P(Y|X,Z)·P(Z) is a product of two manifest factors, so it is recoverable iff BOTH the conditional AND the covariate marginal P(Z) are: the covariate_recovery sub-block carries the P(Z) verdict (null when Z is empty) and the estimand sub-block the combined multi-factor verdict. recoverable=false means 'not via ordered factorization', not a proof of non-recoverability.

target.description: The conditional analyzed, e.g. 'P(y | x, z)'.

recoverable.description: Whether the ADJUSTED CONDITIONAL P(Y|X,given,Z) is recoverable. The full-estimand verdict is estimand.recoverable.

partially_observed.description: The substantive variables that are sometimes missing (V_m).

factorization.description: The recovering ordered factorization: one entry per factor P(factor | conditioned_on, R=0). Empty when not recoverable.

adjustment_set.description: The back-door adjustment set Z whose marginal P(Z) the estimand also needs. Empty when no adjustment is required.

covariate_recovery.description: Recoverability of the covariate marginal P(Z | given). null when the adjustment set Z is empty (no marginal to recover).

estimand.description: The full interventional estimand P(Y | do(X)[, given]) = Σ_z P(Y|X,Z)·P(Z): recoverable iff BOTH the conditional and the covariate marginal are. This is the headline multi-factor verdict.

requires.description: The manifest factors the estimand is built from.

iv_identification.description: Phase 6.iv: metadata emitted when identify / effect is resolved via the IV strategy. The identification only establishes existence of a strategy — the specific formula (Wald / 2SLS / LATE) requires an estimation-layer assumption not captured here.

instrument.description: String form of the chosen instrument atom.

conditioning.description: Sorted list of atom strings forming the conditioning set W (empty = basic IV, non-empty = conditional IV).

required_assumption.description: Text describing the estimation-layer assumption needed to produce a numeric answer (e.g. monotonicity for LATE, linearity for 2SLS).

alternatives_count.description: Total number of valid (Z, W) IV candidates found by structural search. The chosen one is always the subset-minimal and lexicographically first; this count reports how many alternatives exist.

late_caveat.description: Fix 6 (v0.1.5, audit follow-up): present only on numerically-resolved IV results. Mandatory disclosure that the kernel-emitted value is LATE (average effect among compliers — the subpopulation whose treatment shifts with the instrument), NOT the population ATE. Conflating LATE with ATE is a known IV-deployment pitfall; renderer / agent MUST surface this caveat before stating the number.

numeric.description: Fix 6: Wald LATE numeric breakdown. Present only on numerically-resolved IV results. One entry per stratum of the instrument's conditioning set W, so downstream consumers can sanity-check every component; a marginal instrument gives exactly one stratum of weight 1 with no W values. `late` aggregates as a RATIO OF AVERAGES — outcome_shift / treatment_shift — which weights each stratum by its own complier share and so is the effect among compliers. The plain average of the per-stratum ratios is a different estimand and is deliberately not reported. This is what the theta path computes where the data path writes numeric_estimate.stratified_wald, and both are stated in the section that asks how the number was computed.

conditioning_order.description: The conditioning atoms in topological order. Each stratum's `values` is positionally aligned with this list, and the same order fixes the chain-rule factorization of the stratum weight P(W=w). Empty for a marginal instrument.

strata.description: One entry per assignment of the conditioning set, over the declared domains.

values.description: This stratum's conditioning values, positionally aligned with conditioning_order.

weight.description: P(W=w), by the chain rule over conditioning_order.

outcome_shift.description: Sum over strata of P(w) times the instrument's shift in the outcome.

treatment_shift.description: Sum over strata of P(w) times the instrument's shift in the treatment — the complier share under the declared monotonicity.

scm_counterfactual.description: Deterministic linear-SCM counterfactual (Pearl Primer §4.2). Carries the abducted exogenous values (abducted_noise), the post-intervention values of every relevant variable (counterfactual_values), the target's counterfactual point (target_value), and the citation the route implements (reference). Closed. It was the one container among the six that carry a `reference` whose map stayed open, and what came in through that opening was an `estimated_from_data` flag: one writer, no reader, no declaration, restating what the two derivation rule names already say about whether the coefficients were declared or fitted. A block open to anything cannot report a field nobody decided to carry.

intervention.description: The do() this counterfactual was evaluated under, as the variable and the value it was set to.

causation.description: Probabilities of causation (Tian & Pearl 2000) for a causation query. PN/PS/PNS assumption-free bounds, plus point values when monotonic. Carries the observational joint cells and the two interventional risks (with their provenance) that fed the Tian-Pearl formulas. The three quantities and the joint are the SAME shapes the data path records under numeric_estimate, so they are referenced rather than restated: this block held each of them as a bare open object, and what an open object cannot report is a key nobody declared — thirteen of them were being emitted here.

pn.description: Probability of necessity: lower/upper bounds and (when monotonic) point.

ps.description: Probability of sufficiency: lower/upper bounds and (when monotonic) point.

pns.description: Probability of necessity and sufficiency: lower/upper bounds and (when monotonic) point.

interventional_risk_provenance.description: How P(Y=1|do(X)) was obtained. Structural (run) path: 'derived_identification' (from theta via effect identification) or 'user_experimental' (randomized-experiment data, the Tian-Pearl drug case). Data (estimate) path additionally distinguishes 'exogenous' (no back-door path → do-risk = P(Y|X)), 'backdoor_adjustment' (g-formula standardized over a measured set), 'general_id_plug_in' (no adjustment set exists; the general ID algorithm identifies each arm and the estimand is evaluated non-parametrically), and 'instrument_response_polytope' (no arm is point-identified at all; PN/PS/PNS are bounded directly over the response-type distributions reproducing P(X, Y | Z), so p_y_do_x1 / p_y_do_x0 are null).

instrument.description: The instrument column PN/PS/PNS were bounded over, and null on every route that did not use one. Non-null exactly when interventional_risk_provenance is 'instrument_response_polytope'.

observational_joint.description: The four P(X=x, Y=y) cells recovered from theta.

llm_proposed_review.description: Fix 3+4 §3.2 (v0.1.5): aggregated audit surface listing every LLM-proposed element in the program (cause edges tagged annotations.source containing 'llm' + probability statements with provenance='llm_prior'). Attached only when at least one such element exists, so single-population non-LLM-prior runs serialise byte-identically to pre-fix. The Skill v3 contract requires the agent's reply to lead with this list before stating any numeric answer.

edges.description: LLM-proposed causal edges. Each entry has from / to atom strings + the verbatim source string (e.g. 'llm_proposal').

probabilities.description: LLM-proposed probability priors. Each entry has the canonical P(...|...) key, the proposed value, the one-sentence reason (validated non-empty by llm_prior_requires_source), and optional population label.

summary.description: One-sentence human-readable summary the agent must surface in its reply before stating the answer. Counts N edges + M probabilities and reminds the user to audit before trusting the result.

mediation_decomposition.description: Phase 6.mediation: decomposition metadata emitted for effect queries that carry a mediator atom. Reports structural identifiability of NDE/NIE and CDE separately; the chosen strategy picks the strongest identifiable form.

mediator.description: String form of the mediator atom.

mediator_valid.description: True iff the mediator lies on some directed X → ... → M → ... → Y path. False means the mediator declaration is structurally incompatible with the graph.

strategy.description: The strongest identifiable decomposition: nde_nie if Pearl 2001 four conditions hold, else cde if backdoor on (X,M) is available, else none. Absent when mediator_valid=false.

adjustment.description: Sorted list of atom strings forming the adjustment set W used to make M1-M4 hold. Empty list when identifiable with no adjustment, or when not identifiable.

failed_condition.description: First Pearl 2001 condition that blocks identification (null when identifiable).

assumptions.description: Assumptions the structural NDE/NIE identifiability claim rests on (Pearl 2001 cross-world conditions, sequential ignorability, no intermediate confounder, consistency). Empty when not identifiable. IDs reuse the renderer assumption glossary.

adjustment.description: Sorted list of atom strings forming the backdoor adjustment set W for CDE.

failed_condition.description: First CDE backdoor condition that blocks identification (null when identifiable).

assumptions.description: Assumptions the structural CDE identifiability claim rests on (mediator-outcome backdoor adjustment given treatment, consistency). Empty when not identifiable. IDs reuse the renderer assumption glossary.

numeric.description: v0.1.4 Fix 1: numeric mediation evaluation against theta. Boolean-treatment MVP. NDE/NIE branch (when nde_nie is identifiable) reports E[Y(treated)], E[Y(control)], E[Y(treated, M(control))] and the derived TE / NDE-at-control / NIE-at-treated. CDE branch (when cde is identifiable) reports per-mediator-value CDE values. Each branch's failure is recorded as nde_nie_status / cde_status with an insufficient_theta diagnostic. This is the decomposition itself, not a note about it: the headline carries TE alone, and the direct and indirect arms can point opposite ways.

e_y_cross_treated_outer.description: E[Y(X=treated, M = M(X=control))] — cross-world potential with treated outer arm.

e_y_cross_control_outer.description: E[Y(X=control, M = M(X=treated))] — cross-world potential with control outer arm. Needed for the alternative Pearl decomposition TE = NDE_at_treated + NIE_at_control.

nde_at_treated.description: Pearl decomposition with control reference. TE = NDE_at_treated + NIE_at_control.

nie_at_control.description: Pearl decomposition with control reference. Counterpart of nie_at_treated.

nde_nie_status.description: Why this branch produced no numbers. Present exactly when the natural-effect arm was attempted and a constituent formula found theta short.

cde_status.description: Why the controlled arm produced no numbers — theta short at one reference point, or a reference grid past the cap. The two count fields belong to the second case and were being emitted through an open map that could not report them.

reference_point_count.description: Size of the Cartesian product of the mediator block's domains.

cap.description: The size past which the grid is not reported.

transport_identification.description: Which two populations the answer crosses, what differs between them, and the re-weighting that closes the gap. `kind` restates the block's own name and is kept because a writer already emits it. `numeric` appears only once the transport formula has been evaluated against a distribution.

source_population.description: Null when the graph declares no selection node, which is also when there is nothing to transport across.

s_nodes.description: The selection nodes: where the two populations differ, and on which variable each difference acts.

joint_identification.description: How a do() over a treatment SET was identified. `pattern` is a closed vocabulary of two and is NOT the vocabulary `identification.pattern` names, despite the shared field name: the two sets are disjoint, and both reader surfaces branch on `joint_general_id` by spelling the literal, which is what an undeclared domain buys. `interaction` names the scale the treatment x treatment term is stated on; both surfaces currently test only its presence, so a second member would be printed as if it were the first.

adjustment_set.description: Absent on the general-ID route, which is identified precisely because no adjustment set exists.

mediation_joint_decomposition.description: The same decomposition as `mediation_decomposition`, through a mediator SET taken as one block — which is what makes it identifiable without ordering the set. The two arms and the numeric evaluation are the single-mediator ones: the same identifier fills them and the same evaluator computes them, so they are referenced rather than restated. `strategy` is the one thing that genuinely differs: this route can find BOTH arms identifiable and says so, which is the member the single-mediator vocabulary has no room for — and, measured over the whole suite, the only value this field has ever taken.

proximal_estimand.description: The bridge-function estimand proximal identification produces from two proxies of an unmeasured confounder. `method` is a method name rather than a vocabulary — one value per estimator, growing with estimators — so it is typed and not enumerated. `data_conditions` is a joined string because this descriptor rides a derivation step's inputs, whose serializer takes scalars and atoms but not a collection of plain strings.

counterfactual_cell.description: The display copy of `numeric_estimate.counterfactual_cell` — the producer writes ONE dict into both places, so this is a reference to that shape rather than a second statement of it. A second statement is how the same field came to carry `general_id_plug_in` in one place and not in its neighbour.

mechanism_audit.description: The functional form the number was computed under, and where that form came from. `provenance` is the assumption ledger's own vocabulary — this block is one of the channels the ledger reads — so it is declared with the same members. `form` and `method` are NOT vocabularies: one value per estimator, growing whenever an estimator is added, so enumerating them would turn adding an estimator into a validation failure. They are, however, printed to the reader as written, which is a translation question this schema cannot answer. The block is absent, not empty, when the estimator assumed no functional form at all: a mechanism audit that found nothing to audit is a different thing from an audit that was not run, and only one of the two is worth a row headed 'the functional form is'.

assumptions.description: Glossary ids, and a SUBSET of `numeric_estimate.assumptions` — the ones the glossary files under the functional_form layer. A mechanism does not introduce an assumption; it points at the shape choice among those the estimator already declared. This field was one hand-written sentence, which could point at nothing checkable: the ledger's one deduplication is keyed on the assumption id, so the same fact reached the reader twice, in two wordings and — because a sentence cannot be asked which layer it belongs to — under two layers and two severities.

ambiguities.description: The upstream naming ambiguities that bear on THIS query, copied across from the program's own extensions side-channel. Deliberately the one block left open: what it carries is authored upstream by a user or a language model, not by the kernel, and enumerating `kind` would make the kernel the authority on which ambiguities a caller is allowed to report. `kind` is required because an entry that does not say what sort of ambiguity it is cannot be acted on.

type_reconciliation.description: What was checked when the declared variable types and the data's own types disagreed, and what the disagreement was. Four closed vocabularies leave the kernel here: the declared scale, the scale the column actually shows, the coarse dtype family the classification was made from, and the verdict. `ok` is not a member of `verdict` — a reconciliation that agrees is dropped rather than shipped, so a verdict that reaches a reader is always a disagreement. The verifier re-derives the observed scale and the verdict from `n_unique` and `dtype_kind` independently, which is why those two ride along.

declared_scale.description: What the program declared. `nominal` is `discrete` plus the claim that the levels have no order; `observed_scale` beside it has no such member because no column can show it.

observed_scale.description: What the column turned out to be, from cardinality and dtype alone. Three members rather than the declaration's four: whether levels have an order is not a property this can read off the data.

observed_values.description: The distinct values when the column has few enough to record; null otherwise.

unit.description: Never produced by the kernel: no estimator sets one. It survives a caller's decode -> encode round trip, and one verifier rule compares it, which is why it is declared and why it is absent rather than null.

confidence.description: Composite confidence score for the whole result; not a statistical confidence interval.

formula.description: Absent when there is no estimand to state. The null branch this used to allow was never produced — the serializer writes the key only when a formula exists — and a second way to say the same nothing is a way for two producers to disagree.

framing_notes.description: Slice A0 advisory channel: per-predicate gaps in variableDeclaration metadata for predicates referenced by the query. Advisory only — does not influence status.

confidence_sources.description: Slice #34. One entry per slot that participated in the confidence min aggregation, carrying the source annotation, the slot's minimum confidence, and an is_weakest flag marking sources tied with the composite minimum. Absent when no slot contributed or the query is structural.

derivation.description: Machine-verifiable reasoning chain. Only present when the runtime attached one (identify / effect / probability / cause / assoc). Constrained to the exact derivation.schema.json shape so an external agent can round-trip through derivation_from_dict and re-run the verifier.

outcome_error.description: What a declared classical additive measurement-error variance on a CONTINUOUS outcome (Y = Y* + V, E[V|design] = 0) costs this query. Present only when the caller supplied estimate(measurement_error={<outcome>: {error_variance}}) and the answer was reached on one of the designs ``design_kind`` names. It carries no correction and displaces no estimator: such an error leaves every conditional mean unchanged, so the point estimate here is the ordinary one and is already right. What it does carry is the price — the observed residual variance split into signal and measurement noise, and the factor by which that noise widens every least-squares interval on this design. That factor is the part of the uncertainty more subjects cannot buy back, only better measurement. Its ``assumptions`` (chiefly that the error is NON-DIFFERENTIAL, without which the point is not immune after all) are folded into extensions.assumption_ledger, so they land on the surface the report leads with rather than in a side block each consumer must remember to read.

design_kind.description: Which design's residual the declared σ²_v was priced against, and therefore what every other field in this block has to be read against: which residual absorbs σ²_v, which conditioning set the classical premise has to hold on (on ``instrumental_variable`` it is not the design at all but the instrument, so ``assumptions`` names that instrument instead), and whether ``se_inflation`` is the factor or a ceiling on it. There is deliberately no companion field recording that last fact — it is a function of this name, and a second record of it would be free to disagree.

design_vars.description: The design D the outcome's residual is taken around: the exposure, then one drop-first indicator per non-reference mediator level (named "<mediator>=<level>", present only on ``front_door``, because that is the span the front-door outcome model is fitted on and a coarser one would understate the cost), then the adjustment / conditioning set, in topological order. The instrument is NOT here: it names a premise, not a column the residual is taken around.

residual_variance.description: Var(Y − b'D) of the OBSERVED outcome around the design coefficients recorded in sufficient_statistics: the linear projection on D where every coefficient is fitted, the STRUCTURAL residual where the exposure's coefficient was supplied by the estimator that answered (``instrumental_variable``). Taking it around the projection there would price a model nobody fitted.

signal_variance.description: Var(Y*|D) = residual_variance − error_variance: what is left of the unexplained variation once the declared measurement noise is removed. Strictly positive — a non-positive value means the declared variance does not fit under the data, which is refused rather than reported.

se_inflation.description: sqrt(residual_variance / signal_variance): the factor by which the outcome's measurement noise widens the standard error of every least-squares functional of this design, i.e. the reported interval divided by the interval the same design would have produced on a perfectly measured outcome. On ``front_door`` it is an UPPER BOUND rather than the factor, because that design's influence function carries the outcome residual in only one of its terms and the others gain no σ²_v to inflate. Which of the two it is follows from design_kind and is recorded nowhere else.

data_columns.description: The columns ``data_hash`` was taken over, in the order it walked them — the denominator of the fingerprint recorded beside it. Not a second spelling of ``design_vars``: that one names the design the residual is taken around, this one names what the digest covers, and the two differ whenever a column entered the estimate without entering the design.

source.description: Provenance of the declared error variance (validation study / repeat-measurement substudy), as supplied by the caller.

sufficient_statistics.description: Σ_D, Cov(D, Y), Var(Y), the design coefficients, σ²_v and n — the split is a closed-form function of these, so verify_outcome_error re-derives every reported number without the raw data.

design_coefficients.description: The vector b the residual was taken around, in design_vars order. Recorded because it is not always the OLS solution: on ``instrumental_variable`` its first entry is the coefficient the estimator that answered supplied, and only the remaining entries solve the normal equations. A verifier that re-solved for b instead would agree with the producer exactly where the producer happened to solve too, which is the one route where agreement proves nothing.

numeric_estimate.description: Phase 7: data-based estimate. For backdoor / front-door / IV queries this is a single ATE point + CI. For mediation queries it carries a ``decomposition`` sub-block with NDE/NIE/TE triples (point + CI each).

data_columns.description: The columns ``data_hash`` was taken over, in the order it walked them — the denominator that makes the digest a claim about something. The hash mixes each column's NAME and then its values, so on its own a digest that differs says only 'not the same run': not whether what changed was the measurements or the set of columns that entered them. Present exactly when the hash is. This is the set THIS estimator was handed, which is narrower than estimation_context.data_columns wherever the program declared a variable this query does not use — and it is the narrow one that answers 'which columns is this number standing on'.

instruments.description: iv_2sls_overid only: the q >= 2 instruments jointly used in over-identified 2SLS (all valid under the same conditioning set). The just-identified paths use the singular `instrument` instead.

first_stage_f_stat.description: iter 120 / IV methods only: first-stage F-statistic for the instrument's effect on treatment after partialing out conditioning W. Stock & Yogo (2005) flag F < 10 as the canonical weak-instrument threshold. Single-instrument for iv_wald / iv_2sls; the JOINT first-stage F for all instruments under iv_2sls_overid. ABSENT when the computation was degenerate (n too small, instrument variance ~0) — the producer omits it rather than writing null, and this said null until someone read the producer.

stratified_wald.description: iv_stratified_wald only: the per-cell table the point was aggregated from. The aggregate is the RATIO OF AVERAGES — sum_w P(w)*outcome_shift(w) divided by sum_w P(w)*treatment_shift(w) — so each stratum enters weighted by its own complier share (the denominator term, Abadie 2003). That is what makes the point an effect among compliers. Averaging the per-stratum ratios instead weights by P(w) and is a DIFFERENT estimand; the two agree only when the instrument moves treatment equally hard in every stratum, so do not recompute a simple average as a cross-check.

conditioning_order.description: Column names of W in the order each stratum's `values` are listed.

treatment_shift.description: Denominator: sum_w P(w) * treatment_shift(w). This is also the reported complier share — a LATE is an effect on a subpopulation, and this is its size.

values.description: This cell's W values, aligned to conditioning_order.

weight.description: P(W = values) in the sample. Weights sum to 1 across strata; a shortfall would mean the average runs over a narrower population than the query asked about.

treatment_shift.description: E[X|Z=1,w] - E[X|Z=0,w] — this stratum's own complier share.

shift_var_yy.description: Sampling variance of this stratum's outcome_shift, summed over the two instrument arms as V(Y)/n per arm. Together with shift_var_xy / shift_var_xx it gives Var(outcome_shift - beta*treatment_shift) = shift_var_yy - 2*beta*shift_var_xy + beta^2*shift_var_xx, which is what stratified_anderson_rubin_confidence_set inverts.

shift_var_xy.description: Covariance term of the same quadratic — Cov(X,Y)/n summed over the two arms. Not sign-constrained.

shift_var_xx.description: Sampling variance of this stratum's treatment_shift, V(X)/n summed over the two arms.

over_identification.description: iv_2sls_overid only: the over-identification test(s) of the q instruments' JOINT validity. sargan_* is the homoskedastic Sargan (1958); hansen_* (present when the robust weight matrix was non-singular) is its heteroskedasticity-robust efficient-two-step-GMM generalisation, the Hansen (1982) J, which uses the robust weight Ŝ and is the more defensible falsification under heteroskedasticity / clustering. A small p-value REFUTES the joint exclusion restrictions — the linear / continuous analogue of the Balke-Pearl instrumental inequalities; the data refute the instrument set. sufficient_statistics carries the residualised second moments (plus Ŝ when Hansen was computed) that the point + both J statistics are closed forms of, so verify_iv_overid_numeric re-derives everything without the raw data.

hansen_j.description: Heteroskedasticity-robust (efficient two-step GMM) Hansen (1982) J; present when the robust weight matrix Ŝ was non-singular. Coincides with sargan_j under homoskedasticity.

hansen_gmm_point.description: The efficient two-step GMM coefficient on the treatment (byproduct of the Hansen J). The headline `point` stays 2SLS; the two coincide under homoskedasticity.

sufficient_statistics.description: Residualised (FWL, on [1, W]) second moments: Z'Z (q x q), Z'x (q), Z'y (q), and the scalars x'x / x'y / y'y, plus n / n_exog (|W|) / q. When Hansen J was computed, also s_robust: the (q x q) robust weight matrix Ŝ = (1/n) Σ û_i² z_i z_i' (cluster-robust sum under a declared cluster). When the heteroskedasticity-robust AR set was computed, also s0/s1/s2: the three (q x q) matrices with Ŝ(β0) = s0 − β0·s1 + β0²·s2 the robust GMM weight at any β0, from which verify_iv_overid_numeric re-evaluates AR_r(β0).

s_robust.description: The (q x q) robust GMM weight matrix Ŝ; present iff hansen_* is.

s0.description: The (q x q) β0⁰ coefficient of Ŝ(β0); present iff the robust AR set is.

s1.description: The (q x q) β0¹ coefficient of Ŝ(β0); present iff the robust AR set is.

s2.description: The (q x q) β0² coefficient of Ŝ(β0); present iff the robust AR set is.

measurement_correction.description: measurement_error_correction (outcome) / exposure_measurement_error_correction (binary exposure) / combined_measurement_error_correction (both) only: de-attenuation of a misclassified variable by inverting a validated confusion matrix per back-door stratum. OUTCOME side: invert M on the outcome margin (Rogan-Gladen for the binary case). EXPOSURE side (`side` = 'exposure'): the matrix method — invert M on the exposure margin of the (X, Y) joint per stratum, then standardise the recovered true exposure; there is no naive/det shortcut, and `sufficient_statistics.strata` carries full 2xk joint tables instead of per-arm value-count vectors. COMBINED (`side` = 'combined'): both channels are misclassified, so the same 2xk joint is inverted on BOTH sides at once, P_true = M_x^-1 P_obs (M_y^-1)^T; the two matrices are carried separately as `confusion_matrix_exposure` / `confusion_matrix_outcome` (there is no single `confusion_matrix` or `det`) and it requires the two error mechanisms to be independent given the truth, X ⊥ Y | (X*, Y*, Z), which neither single-channel correction assumes. Under NON-differential misclassification a single `confusion_matrix` (+ `det`) applies everywhere. Under DIFFERENTIAL misclassification (`differential` = true) those are replaced by `confusion_matrices`: per-exposure-arm matrices (outcome side / detection bias), per-outcome-level matrices (exposure side / recall bias), or per-covariate-stratum matrices on either side (`differential_by` names the covariate), and the inversion uses the level-specific matrix; a combined correction is never differential. `point` (top-level) is the corrected effect on the target value; `naive_point` is the attenuated back-door number the correction replaces. verify_measurement_correction_numeric (outcome) / verify_exposure_measurement_correction_numeric (exposure) / verify_combined_measurement_correction_numeric (combined) re-inverts the point from sufficient_statistics without the raw data.

side.description: Which margin the channel sits on. Absent (or 'outcome') for the outcome correction; 'exposure' for the binary-exposure matrix method; 'combined' when both are misclassified and the joint is inverted on both sides.

det.description: det(M) — non-differential only; absent under differential (there is no single matrix).

out_of_simplex.description: True if any recovered p_true=M^-1 p_obs landed outside [0,1] — a signal the matrix is weakly informative or non-differential is violated. The point is still the method-of-moments estimator (unclipped).

confusion_matrix.description: Non-differential, single-channel only. Column-stochastic: M[i][j] = P(observed=states[i] | true=states[j]). k x k over the outcome states (outcome side) or 2 x 2 over the exposure states (exposure side).

confusion_matrix_exposure.description: Combined only: the 2 x 2 exposure channel, M_x[i][j] = P(X=states[i] | X*=states[j]).

confusion_matrix_outcome.description: Combined only: the k x k outcome channel, M_y[i][j] = P(Y=outcome_states[i] | Y*=outcome_states[j]).

det_joint.description: Combined only: det(M_x)^k · det(M_y)^2, the determinant of the composed 2k x 2k map — how much information the two channels destroy together, which neither det reports alone.

confusion_matrices.description: Differential only: the per-conditioning-level matrices the inversion used. Outcome side (detection bias): one entry per exposure arm (`arm`). Outcome side by a COVARIATE: one entry per covariate level (`level`), with `differential_by` naming the covariate. Exposure side (recall bias): one entry per outcome level (`outcome`). Exposure side by a COVARIATE: one entry per covariate level (`level`), with `differential_by` naming the covariate.

level.description: Differential by a covariate (outcome or exposure side): the covariate value this matrix applies to.

differential_by.description: Differential by a COVARIATE: the back-door covariate whose value selects the confusion matrix within each stratum. Absent/default = the exposure arm (outcome side) or the outcome (exposure side).

states.description: The confusion-matrix states: outcome states (outcome side) or the two exposure states in [control, treated] order (exposure side).

outcome_states.description: exposure / combined side only: the k outcome states in the joint-table column order.

sufficient_statistics.description: Everything the numeric verifier re-inverts. Outcome side: the confusion matrix (non-differential), per-arm matrices (`confusion_matrices_by_arm`, detection bias), or per-covariate-stratum matrices (`confusion_matrices_by_level` + `differential_by`), per-(arm, stratum) outcome value-count vectors, covariate marginal counts. Exposure side: the confusion matrix (non-differential), per-outcome matrices (`confusion_matrices_by_outcome`, recall bias), or per-covariate-stratum matrices (`confusion_matrices_by_level` + `differential_by`), per-stratum full 2xk (X, Y) joint tables (`joint_counts`), the outcome states, and the covariate marginal counts. Combined side: both channels' matrices (`exposure_confusion_matrix` / `outcome_confusion_matrix`) with their dets and the composed map's `det_joint`, over the same per-stratum 2xk joint tables.

exposure_confusion_matrix.description: Combined only: the 2x2 exposure channel M_x.

outcome_confusion_matrix.description: Combined only: the k x k outcome channel M_y.

det_joint.description: Combined only: det(M_x)^k · det(M_y)^2, the determinant of the composed map.

differential.description: True under differential misclassification: the single confusion_matrix/det are absent and replaced by the per-level matrices below.

confusion_matrices_by_arm.description: Differential outcome side (detection bias): one column-stochastic matrix per exposure arm.

differential_by.description: Differential (outcome OR exposure side) by a COVARIATE: the back-door covariate whose value selects the matrix within each stratum. The verifier finds it via adjustment_vars and reads the value from each stratum's z.

confusion_matrices_by_level.description: Differential (outcome OR exposure side) by a COVARIATE: one column-stochastic matrix per covariate level (must cover every observed value of differential_by).

confusion_matrices_by_outcome.description: Differential exposure side (recall bias): one column-stochastic 2x2 matrix per outcome level.

outcome_states.description: exposure side only: the k outcome states in joint-table column order.

oneOf.description: Outcome side: one record per (arm, covariate stratum) with the full outcome value-count vector.
Exposure side: one record per covariate stratum with the full 2xk (X, Y) joint count table (row 0 = control exposure, row 1 = treated exposure; columns = outcome states).

regression_calibration.description: regression_calibration only: de-attenuation of one or more continuously-mismeasured design columns (classical additive error W = V + U with a known error variance sigma^2_u) by the regression-calibration moment correction beta_true = (Sigma_obs - E)^-1 Sigma_obs b_naive, with E = diag(sigma^2_u placed on each mismeasured column, 0 elsewhere). The mismeasured column may be the EXPOSURE (regression dilution -> attenuation) and/or a back-door COVARIATE (imperfect adjustment -> residual confounding, a bias in either direction). `point` (top-level) is the corrected per-unit exposure slope beta_x on the true exposure X* adjusting for the true Z; `naive_point` is the biased naive back-door OLS slope the correction replaces. `reliability` lambda = 1 - sigma^2_u / Var(W|Z) is the EXPOSURE's continuous analogue of det(M) (1.0 when the exposure is measured accurately); `error_variances` maps each mismeasured design variable to its sigma^2_uv and `reliabilities` maps each to its lambda_v. verify_regression_calibration_numeric re-derives the corrected/naive slope + reliabilities from sufficient_statistics (the design covariance matrix Sigma_obs + Cov(D,Y) + the error variances) without the raw data.

error_variance.description: The EXPOSURE's error variance sigma^2_u (0.0 when only a covariate is mismeasured).

error_variances.description: Each mismeasured design variable name -> its known classical error variance sigma^2_uv.

reliabilities.description: Each mismeasured design variable name -> its reliability lambda_v = 1 - sigma^2_uv / Var(V|rest).

design_vars.description: The design column order [exposure, ...back-door covariates Z] the covariance matrix and slopes are indexed by; the exposure is index 0.

sufficient_statistics.description: Everything verify_regression_calibration_numeric re-derives the corrected/naive slope from. cov_matrix is the (p x p) sample covariance Sigma_obs of the design (design_vars order, exposure first); cov_design_y is Cov(D, Y); error_variances maps each mismeasured column to sigma^2_uv (E = diag of these at their design indices). From these the naive slope Sigma^-1 cov_design_y, the corrected slope (Sigma - E)^-1 cov_design_y, and each lambda_v = 1 - sigma^2_uv/Var(V|rest) are closed forms.

anderson_rubin_confidence_set.description: iter 212 (single-instrument) / iter 240 (over-identified) — IV methods only: the Anderson-Rubin (1949) weak-identification-robust confidence set for the IV coefficient. Valid regardless of first-stage strength — unlike the bootstrap CI. For a single endogenous regressor (whether just-identified or over-identified with q instruments) it is the solution of a quadratic inequality in beta0 and can be a bounded interval [lower, upper], a disconnected pair (-inf, lower] u [upper, +inf), a single ray, or the whole line (an unbounded shape is the honest signal that the data cannot bound the effect); the OVER-IDENTIFIED set can additionally be empty (no beta0 satisfies all q moment restrictions — an over-identification rejection visible in the set geometry). Under iv_2sls_overid the critical value is kappa = q*F(q, m) and the set is re-derived by verify_iv_overid_numeric from the recorded moment matrices; under the just-identified path kappa = F(1, m) and it is re-derived from the flat ar_* derivation inputs.

lower.description: Finite lower endpoint where it exists; null on an open side. For a disconnected set this is the upper edge of the left ray (-inf, lower].

upper.description: Finite upper endpoint where it exists; null on an open side. For a disconnected set this is the lower edge of the right ray [upper, +inf).

point.description: The IV point the set is centred on — the just-identified Szy/Szx (single instrument) or the 2SLS point P_xy/P_xx (over-identified); null if the first stage is exactly degenerate. NB for the over-identified set the point need not lie inside the set.

kappa.description: iv_2sls_overid only: the AR critical value q*F(q, m) (m = n - |W| - q - 1). Absent on the single-instrument path (its kappa = F(1, m) rides on the ar_kappa derivation input).

dof_num.description: iv_2sls_overid only: numerator df q (number of instruments).

dof_denom.description: iv_2sls_overid only: denominator df m = n - |W| - q - 1.

stratified_anderson_rubin_confidence_set.description: iv_stratified_wald only: the weak-identification-robust confidence set for the STRATIFIED Wald, inverted on that estimand's own moment. anderson_rubin_confidence_set residualises Y, X, Z on [1, W] — the same additive projection that makes 2SLS weight strata by Var(Z|w) — so its point is the linear IV coefficient and it belongs to a different estimand; the two sets are never both present. Here, with A = sum_w P(w)*outcome_shift(w) and B = sum_w P(w)*treatment_shift(w) (the point being A/B), the set is {beta0 : (A - beta0*B)^2 <= kappa * (var_yy - 2*beta0*var_xy + beta0^2*var_xx)} where var_.. = sum_w P(w)^2 * that stratum's shift_var_.. . Same quadratic inversion and therefore the same five shapes; as B -> 0 it opens out to the whole line, which is the honest answer when the instrument moves no compliers. Only the AGGREGATE moment is inverted, not the S per-stratum ones: the estimand IS the ratio of averages, whereas imposing all S moments would test the stronger hypothesis that every stratum shares one LATE — and strata whose LATEs differ are what this estimand averages over. Because the stratum variances are arm-specific, the set does not assume homoskedasticity across arms or strata; with unbalanced instrument arms that matters in both directions. Re-solved by the verifier from the stratum table, which carries the same quantities per cell.

lower.description: Finite lower endpoint where it exists; null on an open side. For a disconnected set this is the upper edge of the left ray (-inf, lower].

upper.description: Finite upper endpoint where it exists; null on an open side. For a disconnected set this is the lower edge of the right ray [upper, +inf).

point.description: A/B — which on this path IS the reported point estimate, not a second number. A set centred anywhere else would be a confidence set for one estimand beside a point for another, and the verifier rejects that.

kappa.description: F(1, dof) critical value. A finite-sample refinement, conservative relative to the asymptotic chi^2(1) the arm-robust variance strictly justifies — wider, never narrower.

outcome_shift.description: A = sum_w P(w) * outcome_shift(w); equals stratified_wald.outcome_shift.

treatment_shift.description: B = sum_w P(w) * treatment_shift(w); equals stratified_wald.treatment_shift, the complier share.

n_strata.description: S — must equal the length of the stratified_wald.strata array.

dof.description: n - 2*S: two cell means per stratum.

robust_anderson_rubin_confidence_set.description: iter 246 / iv_2sls_overid only: the HETEROSKEDASTICITY-ROBUST Anderson-Rubin confidence set (Stock-Wright 2000 S-statistic / Kleibergen 2005 robust AR) — valid under weak identification AND heteroskedasticity (or clustering) at once, where the homoskedastic anderson_rubin_confidence_set has the wrong weighting (the same defect Sargan has vs the robust Hansen J). It inverts AR_r(β0) = n·ḡ(β0)'Ŝ(β0)⁻¹ḡ(β0) ~ χ²(q) with the β0-dependent robust weight Ŝ(β0) = s0 − β0·s1 + β0²·s2. Because AR_r is not a ratio of quadratics, the set is the real roots of a degree-≤2q polynomial (exact, not a grid) and is reported as a list of segments; it can be bounded, disconnected (two rays), the whole line, empty, or a union of more than two pieces. Both tails share the finite asymptote (1/n)·zx'·s2⁻¹·zx, which governs whether the set is unbounded (asymptote ≤ crit → the honest weak-identification signal). verify_iv_overid_numeric re-evaluates AR_r from the recorded s0/s1/s2 and independently re-checks the crossings, asymptote, segments, and completeness.

segments.description: The set as a list of intervals; lower/upper null on an open side.

crossings.description: Sorted finite boundary points where AR_r(β0) = crit.

asymptote.description: The shared tail value (1/n)·zx'·s2⁻¹·zx of AR_r as β0 → ±∞.

point.description: The 2SLS point the polynomial root search is centred on; need not lie inside the set.

cluster_robust.description: True if Ŝ(β0) used the cluster-robust (CR0) sum under a declared cluster; else HC0.

treatment_high.description: general_id_plugin only: the high treatment level the ATE contrasts do(X=treatment_high) against do(X=treatment_low).

treatment_low.description: general_id_plugin only: the low (reference) treatment level of the ATE contrast.

outcome_high.description: general_id_plugin only: the outcome level the binary P(Y=outcome_high|do(X)) contrast is taken on.

given.description: general_id_idc_plugin only: the Z=z stratum the conditional ATE P(Y|do(X),Z=z) is taken within. Each entry is a [predicate, value] pair.

conditional.description: ctf_conjunction_plugin only: whether the estimand is a conditional P(γ|δ) (IDC*) rather than an unconditional P(γ) (ID*).

estimand.description: ctf_conjunction_plugin only: a human-readable rendering of the identified counterfactual probability, e.g. P(y_{x=True}=True | x=False).

treatments.description: Joint interventions: the full treatment vector {A, B, ...} intervened on simultaneously. Present for joint_backdoor_* methods and joint_general_id_plugin.

target.description: scm_counterfactual_linear_fit only: the counterfactual target variable Y whose value under the intervention is computed for the unit.

intervention_var.description: scm_counterfactual_linear_fit only: the intervened variable X in do(X=value).

intervention_value.description: scm_counterfactual_linear_fit only: the value x the intervention pins X to.

node_fits.description: scm_counterfactual_linear_fit only: the per-node fitted linear structural equations + the OLS moment matrices verify_scm_counterfactual_numeric independently re-solves. One entry per relevant endogenous node (the intervened variable excluded). xtx / xty are the augmented normal-equation moments over the design [1, parents].

observed_unit.description: scm_counterfactual_linear_fit only: the unit's factual values (Pearl's E=e) over the relevant set as [variable, value] pairs, in topological order — the abduction input.

joint_effect.description: Joint interventions: the joint g-formula contrast E[Y|do(treated)] − E[Y|do(control)] over the treatment vector, with the cells it was taken between. Present only for joint_backdoor_* methods.

interaction.description: Joint interventions: the highest-order (K-way) causal interaction on the additive (difference) scale — the K-th mixed finite difference over the 2^K treatment corners, Σ_s (−1)^{#lo(s)} E[Y|do(s)] (VanderWeele 2015 ch.14). For K=2 treatments this is the ordinary treatment×treatment interaction [do(1,1)−do(1,0)] − [do(0,1)−do(0,0)]. Present only for joint_backdoor_* methods; ``order`` gives K.

order.description: The interaction order K = number of treatments in the joint vector (the finite difference is K-th order).

interaction_unavailable.description: Present instead of `interaction` when some corner of the treatment box has no rows. The K-way interaction is a finite difference over all 2^K corners, so an empty corner leaves it unidentified — the outcome model would still predict there, and the number would be an extrapolation reported as a measurement. The joint contrast is unaffected whenever its own two cells (all-treated, all-control) are observed, which is why it is still present. `unsupported_cells` names the empty corners.

order.description: The interaction order K that could not be estimated.

unsupported_cells.description: The treatment cells with no rows, each a {treatment: value} map.

treatment_proxy.description: proximal_matrix only: the treatment-inducing proxy Z (negative-control exposure).

outcome_proxy.description: proximal_matrix only: the outcome-inducing proxy W (negative-control outcome).

latent_cardinality.description: proximal_matrix only: the assumed number k of categories of the unobserved confounder U.

do_prob_treated.description: proximal_matrix only: P(Y=1|do(X=1)) recovered by Miao formula (5).

do_prob_control.description: proximal_matrix only: P(Y=1|do(X=0)) recovered by Miao formula (5).

probabilities_of_causation.description: causation_plugin only: the full PN/PS/PNS answer (Tian-Pearl 2000) from data. Each of pn/ps/pns carries its assumption-free bounds (lower/upper) and, under monotonicity, the point + its bootstrap CI. The top-level numeric_estimate point/ci mirror pn (the necessity headline).

adjustment.description: The back-door adjustment set standardized over for the do-risks (empty for exogenous / experimental / general-ID / instrument).

instrument.description: The instrument column the three quantities were bounded over, and null on every route that did not use one. Non-null exactly when interventional_risk_provenance is 'instrument_response_polytope': no interventional risk is point-identified, so PN/PS/PNS are optimised directly over the response-type distributions reproducing P(X, Y | Z) rather than read off Tian-Pearl's closed form.

counterfactual_cell.description: counterfactual_cell_plugin only: the single binary counterfactual cell P(Y_{x'}=y*|X=x[,Y=y]) recovered from data. lower/upper is the identified set; point is non-null exactly when it collapsed (the same-world consistency case, the ETT identity when no factual outcome is given, or an interval a declared monotonicity pinned). ci_lower/ci_upper is the point's percentile bootstrap CI when point-identified, and otherwise the OUTER band on [lower, upper] (Manski / Balke-Pearl data-bounds convention). p_y_do_x_cf is the ONE interventional arm this cell depends on — null exactly when the answer does not use one, which interventional_risk_provenance then justifies. TWO solvers can fill these fields and the provenance says which ran: the consistency identity, which consumes the risk as a scalar, and — where no risk is point-identified but the graph carries an instrument — the response-function linear program, which optimises the cell directly over the distributions reproducing P(X, Y | Z) and has no risk to report. bootstrap_draws_infeasible counts resamples whose empirical inputs admit no SCM under the declared monotonicity: a finite-sample measure of how close that assumption sits to being refuted, on either solver.

observed_x.description: The factual treatment value X = x conditioned on.

counterfactual_x.description: The intervened value x' in do(X = x').

target_y.description: The counterfactual outcome value y* whose probability is asked for.

factual_y.description: The factual outcome y when it is part of the evidence; null makes the cell the ETT identity, which is point-identified outright.

adjustment.description: The back-door adjustment set standardized over for the do-risk (empty for exogenous / experimental / general-ID / no-risk-needed).

instrument.description: The instrument column the cell was bounded over, and null on every route that did not use one. Non-null exactly when interventional_risk_provenance is 'instrument_response_polytope': no interventional risk is point-identified, so the cell is optimised directly over the response-type distributions reproducing P(X, Y | Z) rather than read off the consistency identity.

ci_width_is.description: Which of the two objects the ci pair holds on THIS run: 'sampling' when a point was identified and the pair is that point's bootstrap interval, 'outer_band' when it was not and the pair is a conservative band on [lower, upper]. Null exactly when nothing was resampled. Written by the estimator, which is what saw which came out — every surface used to recover it from whether ``point`` was null, separately. Vocabulary: themis.intervals.Width.

selection_recovery_numeric.description: selection_backdoor_recovery only (§S9.1 numeric end): the detail behind the ATE recovered from selection bias by the Bareinboim-Pearl selection-backdoor formula (Theorem 3.5). The top-level numeric_estimate point/ci is μ(1)−μ(0); mu_treated/mu_control are the two arms; sufficient_statistics carries the per-stratum biased (n, y_sum) counts and the external unbiased weight tables P(z⁺)/P(z⁻|x,z⁺) that verify_selection_recovery_numeric re-runs the formula on.

reference_data_columns.description: The columns ``reference_data_hash`` was taken over, in the order it walked them — the denominator of the external unbiased table's fingerprint. The biased sample the estimate was recovered FROM is fingerprinted separately, on numeric_estimate.

z_plus.description: Non-descendants of X in the adjustment set (confounding control, weighted by external P(z⁺)).

z_minus.description: Descendants of X in the adjustment set (selection control, reweighted by external P(z⁻|x,z⁺)).

selected_values.description: The value that defines 'selected' for each selection node S the biased sample is restricted on.

mu_treated.description: μ(1) = E[Y|do(X=1)] recovered by the Theorem-3.5 sum.

mu_control.description: μ(0) = E[Y|do(X=0)] recovered by the Theorem-3.5 sum.

sufficient_statistics.description: Audit trail the numeric verifier re-derives the point from: z_plus_vars / z_minus_vars, ref_p_zplus (external P(z⁺) records), ref_p_zminus_given (external P(z⁻|x,z⁺) records), biased_strata (per-(arm, z⁺, z⁻) n + y_sum on the S-restricted sample), and the recomputed mu_treated / mu_control.

sensitivity_analysis.description: Phase 8.2 + iter 124: VanderWeele 2017 E-value sensitivity for the numeric estimate. Present for binary outcomes (RR via baseline rate) and continuous outcomes (RR ≈ exp(0.91·SMD) per Chinn 2000). Categorical / object-typed outcomes silently skip this block. baseline_rate is null on the continuous path because the conversion is fully standardisation-based. path + baseline_rate / outcome_sd record the conversion INPUTS so the verifier (verify_e_value) re-derives the risk ratio and both E-values from the audited headline ATE with a second, independent transcription of the formulas, and re-derives interpretation_band + band_basis from the E-values it just confirmed. The reading is NOT in note: a band said twice can disagree with itself, and prose is the copy nothing re-derives.

outcome_sd.description: Outcome standard deviation used for the Chinn SMD→RR conversion (continuous path); null on the binary path.

path.description: Which ATE→RR conversion produced this block: binary (baseline rate) or continuous (Chinn SMD).

interpretation_band.description: The reading a person acts on: how much unmeasured confounding this result could absorb. Null exactly when e_value is null. The cut-points (1.5 / 2.5 / 5) are Themis's own — VanderWeele & Ding state the quantity and leave the reading to the reader — and which NUMBER they are applied to is the paper's, recorded beside them in band_basis.

band_basis.description: Which E-value the band was read off: the confidence bound nearer the null whenever there is one, and the point estimate only when there is not. Stated rather than left to be inferred — a reader who has to know the rule in order to know what they are being told cannot notice the rule being wrong, and this one was.

ovb_sensitivity.description: Cinelli & Hazlett (2020) omitted-variable-bias sensitivity — the regression-scale complement to the E-value, attached to backdoor_linear estimates. A closed form of the OLS fit's treatment t-value + residual dof: the robustness value (RV_q = confounding strength, as a partial R² shared with BOTH treatment and outcome, needed to reduce the estimate by 100·q%; RV_{q,α} additionally kills significance at α), the partial R² of the treatment with the outcome, and per-covariate benchmark bounds (the confounder strength / bias implied by a confounder kd/ky times as strong as an observed covariate). All fields are re-derivable by the verifier from t_statistic + dof + the per-benchmark partial R²s.

estimate.description: OLS treatment coefficient (equals the g-formula point for a linear no-interaction model).

q.description: Reduction fraction the robustness value targets (q=1 → explain the effect away entirely).

benchmarks.description: One entry per observed covariate benchmarked against. Empty when the adjustment set is empty.

r2dxj_x.description: Partial R² of the treatment with this covariate (the bound input).

r2yxj_dx.description: Partial R² of the outcome with this covariate (the bound input).

r2dz_x.description: Implied R²_{D~Z|X} of a confounder kd times as strong; null when the bound math is undefined (covariate too strong to benchmark).

r2yz_dx.description: Implied R²_{Y~Z|D,X} of a confounder ky times as strong; null when the bound math is undefined.

adjusted_estimate.description: Treatment effect after adjusting for the implied confounder; null when the bound is void (implied R² outside [0,1]).

valid.description: False when the implied confounder R² escapes [0,1] — a covariate too strong to serve as a valid benchmark.

sampling_points.description: Phase 14: T values at which the dose-response curve was evaluated. Sorted ascending; first value is the reference (effect=0 by construction).

reference_point.description: Phase 14: T value used as the reference for curve effect calculations (the smallest sampling point).

dose_response_curve.description: Phase 14: predicted average effect on Y of moving T from reference_point to each sampling_point. Length matches sampling_points; the reference point's row has effect=0.

bootstrap.description: Cluster-bootstrap metadata. Present only when a cluster / block column was supplied (options.cluster): the percentile CI then resamples whole clusters (Cameron-Gelbach-Miller pairs cluster bootstrap) instead of i.i.d. rows, which is the correct variance under within-cluster dependence. Absent ⇒ the default i.i.d. bootstrap.

propensity_summary.description: Doubly-robust / IPW methods (aipw / ipw_*): overlap-positivity disclosure. raw_min/raw_max are the propensity range BEFORE Winsorizing (the honest overlap picture); n_trimmed counts units whose propensity was clipped to the [floor, 1-floor] band to keep the inverse-probability weights finite (large ⇒ thin overlap, NOT hidden). model is 'logistic' (fit on the adjustment set) or 'marginal' (empty adjustment ⇒ e = P(T=1)).

doubly_robust.description: AIPW / TMLE: True. Flags that the estimate is consistent if EITHER the outcome regression OR the propensity model is correctly specified (Robins-Rotnitzky-Zhao 1994; Bang & Robins 2005; van der Laan & Rose 2011).

tmle_epsilon.description: TMLE only: the fluctuation (targeting) parameter ε from the logistic-fluctuation step. A transparency handle — ε near 0 means the initial outcome fit was already well-targeted; a larger |ε| means the targeting step moved the estimate substantially.

std_error.description: AIPW / TMLE: influence-function standard error of the ATE (the analytic-CI path). Null when the CI was skipped. From the efficient influence curve; cluster-robust when a cluster column is in play.

ci_method.description: AIPW / TMLE: how the CI was formed — 'influence_function' is the analytic Wald CI from the efficient influence curve (the default, the doubly-robust estimators' advantage over the bootstrap-only g-formula); 'bootstrap' refits the estimator per resample.

stabilized.description: IPW only: True for the Hajek (stabilized-weights) estimator, False for the raw Horvitz-Thompson form.

longitudinal_gformula.description: Phase 7.L: longitudinal parametric g-formula (g-computation) detail for a time-varying treatment STRATEGY (Hernán & Robins, What If, ch.21). point/ci mirror the top-level fields; the rest exposes the time-ordered treatment + covariate spec, the two simulated strategy means, and the Monte-Carlo / bootstrap budgets so a consumer can audit the always-treat vs never-treat contrast.

longitudinal_ipw_msm.description: Phase 7.L: longitudinal IPW marginal structural model detail for a time-varying treatment STRATEGY (Robins 2000; Hernán & Robins ch.12/17). An independent route to the same strategy contrast as longitudinal_gformula — it models the TREATMENT process (per-time propensities → IP weights) rather than the covariate/outcome models, so agreement between the two cross-validates the estimate. msm_coefficients are (β0, β_A0, …, β_AK) of E[Y_ā]=β0+Σβ_k·a_k; weight_mean/weight_max disclose the weight distribution (a mean far from 1 or a huge max flags near-positivity violation).

recovered_ate.description: Phase 9 §S9.2 numeric end: the back-door ATE recovered from data that itself has missing values (Mohan-Pearl-Tian 2013). Each g-formula factor is estimated from its OWN complete cases — the conditional E[Y|X,Z] from rows with {Y,X,Z} observed, the covariate marginal P(Z) from rows with {Z} observed — so under MAR the estimate is unbiased where naive listwise deletion (naive_listwise_ate, both factors from the fully-complete subset) is not. n_conditional_rows / n_marginal_rows expose the two factor-specific complete-case sizes; their gap is why the multi-factor combination matters.

naive_listwise_ate.description: The biased complete-case comparison (both factors from the listwise-deleted subset); null when that subset has an empty treatment×stratum cell.

sufficient_statistics.description: Per-stratum sufficient statistics the g-formula sum was built from — the record verify_missing_data_numeric re-derives Σ_z (E[Y|1,z]−E[Y|0,z])·P(z) from without re-touching the data. `recovered` (and, when the naive listwise foil exists, `naive`) each carry conditional_strata ({z,arm,n,y_sum} per contributing (arm,z) cell, so E[Y|arm,z]=y_sum/n), marginal_counts ({z,count} per z) and marginal_total (P(z)=count/total). `adjustment_vars` pins the z-key arity.

naive.description: Null when the listwise-deleted foil has an empty cell and no naive comparison exists. Always written — the recovered number means little without saying whether there was anything to compare it against.

decomposition.description: Phase 7.4 mediation decomposition: point + CI for NDE, NIE, TE, plus the proportion of total effect mediated through M (NIE / TE).

proportion_mediated.description: NIE / TE — the fraction of the total effect that flows through the mediator (or, for a mediator SET, through the set as a block). Renderer surfaces this directly as the answer to attribution-flavored questions ('X 占多大份额', '是不是因为 M').

sufficient_statistics.description: Joint multi-mediator decomposition only (method mediation_joint_*): the outcome-model coefficients and per-mediator standardized means from which verify_mediation_numeric re-derives the joint NDE/NIE independently on the linear path (NDE = beta_x + sum_j gamma_j * q_j0; NIE = sum_j (beta_j + gamma_j)(q_j1 - q_j0)).

cde.description: Joint multi-mediator decomposition only (method mediation_joint_*): the controlled direct effect holding the WHOLE mediator block fixed at a reference level, reported at m*=0 (all mediators at control) and m*=1 (all at treated). On the linear path verify_mediation_numeric re-derives CDE(m*=0)=beta_x and CDE(m*=1)=beta_x+sum_j gamma_j from the recorded outcome coefficients; on the logit path it is a plug-in over the covariates (construction ceiling). Attached only when the CDE-for-a-set is structurally identified with the same adjustment the joint model was fit under.

four_way_decomposition.description: VanderWeele 2014 four-way decomposition (Explanation in Causal Inference Ch.14): TE = CDE + INTref + INTmed + PIE, splitting the total effect into the portion due to neither mediation nor interaction (CDE), only interaction (INTref), both (INTmed), and only mediation (PIE). PNDE=CDE+INTref and TNIE=INTmed+PIE reconcile with the nde/nie in `decomposition`. Risk-difference scale; CDE fixes the mediator at reference 0.

sufficient_statistics.description: The standardized cell means the difference-scale split was built from — the sufficient statistics verify_mediation_numeric re-derives every component (and, on the linear-outcome path, NDE/NIE) from, turning the block from invariant-only into a strong re-derivation (the difference-scale analog of four_way_ratio.coefficients). cell_means: p00/p01/p10/p11 = E[Y|A,M] and q0/q1 = E[M|A], g-formula standardized over the sample covariates.

four_way_unavailable.description: Present instead of four_way_decomposition when the difference-scale four-way is invalid for the data shape (continuous mediator under a nonlinear/logit outcome). `reason` explains why.

four_way_ratio.description: VanderWeele 2014 eAppendix §3.4 (binary mediator) / §3.3 (continuous mediator) RATIO-scale (excess relative risk) four-way decomposition, attached to a mediation numeric_estimate when the OUTCOME is binary. For a binary outcome the multiplicative scale is the natural one: the total excess relative risk (total_rr − 1) = err_cde + err_intref + err_intmed + err_pie. Unlike the collapsible difference-scale four_way_decomposition these components are NON-collapsible functions of the logistic outcome coefficients (odds-ratio approximation). mediator_scale is 'binary' (§3.4, logistic mediator) or 'continuous' (§3.3, linear mediator; mediator_residual_variance then carries σ²).

coefficients.description: The fitted outcome / mediator model coefficients the VanderWeele closed form was evaluated at — the sufficient statistics verify_four_way_ratio re-derives every err_* / prop_* from. t1/t2/t3: outcome-model logit coefficients on A / M / A·M; b0/b1: mediator-model intercept / A coefficient; bcc: mediator-model covariate contribution at the sample-mean covariate value; mediator_reference: the m* the CDE fixes M at.

estimation_context.description: Phase 7.1: data contract + option snapshot that gave rise to a numeric_estimate. Helps the verifier reason about reproducibility without access to the raw data.

data_columns.description: The columns ``data_hash`` was taken over, in the order it walked them — the denominator of the fingerprint recorded beside it, and therefore the list a reader compares when two contexts disagree: it separates a change in the measurements from a change in which columns were measured. What ARRIVED, not what any one answer used: it names every predicate the program declared, including the ones no query estimated. Read as the latter it says yes to every column there is, which is how a declared-but-unestimated column once blocked every point estimate in the program; the per-answer sets sit beside their own digests (numeric_estimate.data_columns, boundsResult.numeric_data_columns), and they are narrower.

cluster.description: The cluster / block column resolved for this RUN (explicit kwarg or options.cluster). A run-level inference input like random_state and ci_bootstrap, recorded once before any estimator consumes it: without it the envelope cannot distinguish a run where no cluster column was named from one where an estimator dropped it, so the audit layer demands every interval produced under a clustered run name this column in its own declared assumptions — honoured or explicitly not honoured. Absent when the run named no cluster column.

estimator_failure.description: Phase 14: structured failure when an estimator is reachable but produces an unusable answer (overlap insufficient, convergence failure, etc.). Mutually exclusive with numeric_estimate on the same result. ``not_recoverable`` is the §S9.2 missing-data case (and the §S9.1 selection-backdoor-non-recoverable case): identification decided the estimand cannot be recovered, so the estimator refuses to produce a number. ``external_data_required`` is the §S9.1 selection-bias case where the effect IS recoverable but only with external unbiased data the caller has not supplied (which distributions, and the formula they would feed, are on ``extensions.selection_recovery`` — this block says why there is no number, not what would produce one) — the ordinary (biased) number is withheld rather than shipped.

failure_type.description: Which species of refusal this is. The set is closed and lives in themis/refusals.py. A test holds this list equal to that registry, so a new species cannot reach a consumer without appearing here.

kind.description: What the reader should do about this refusal, stamped from themis/refusals.py rather than written at the site that refused. graph: the structure forbids the quantity — more of the same data will not help. data: the structure permits it and this sample cannot support it. unbuilt: well-posed and identified, not yet built — an honest capability gap. request: an input the caller supplied is malformed or inconsistent; change it and retry. backend: a numeric routine did not return an answer, and no verdict has been passed on the question or the data. Every refusal Themis emits carries it; it is optional here because verify() also accepts envelopes this kernel did not produce.

estimator_dependency_missing.description: Phase 14: surfaces when an optional estimator backend (e.g. EconML for dose-response) isn't installed. Carries the install hint so the caller can resolve.

data_gap_report.description: Phase 10: structured 'what data is still needed to validate this causal claim' summary. ABSENT for query kinds that carry no data needs (cause / assoc) and when no gaps were detected — the serializer writes the key only when there is a report, so the null this used to also allow was never produced. Generator: themis/output/data_gap_report.py — pure function over derivation + investigation_requests + framing_notes + extensions, no I/O.

bounds_results.description: Phase 12: symbolic bounds on the queried estimand when point identification fails. ONE ENTRY PER METHOD whose assumptions the program supports — they bracket the same estimand under assumption sets that do not contain one another (Manski assumes nothing; Balke-Pearl needs IV1/IV2/IV3; Manski-Tamer needs a declared monotone treatment response), so no ranking picks one and a single slot would hold whichever ran first. Do NOT intersect them: both holding means the truth is in both, but the intersection is not the sharp set under the conjunction. Absent when point is identifiable, when no method applies, or for non-effect queries. Generator: themis/output/bounds.py via scheduler._attach_bounds_results.

observationalJoint.description: The four cells of P(X, Y). Three containers carry it — the data path's probabilities_of_causation and counterfactual_cell, and the theta path's extensions.causation — and it means the same thing in all three, so it is declared once. The third container had it as a bare open object, which is why four cells nobody had declared were being emitted through it.

causationQuantity.description: One probability of causation (PN, PS, or PNS) as the structural route reports it: assumption-free bounds (lower/upper) and, under monotonicity, the point. ``point`` is REQUIRED and null when there is none — not omitted. The two routes carrying this quantity used to say 'not point-identified' two different ways, the data one writing null and the structural one leaving the key out, which made the kernel's display-copy cross-check ask about PRESENCE on one path and about the VALUE on the other for the same field. The sampling band is not here: neither writer of this container has ever produced one, and a shape that claims a field nobody fills is a claim about the answer that the answer does not make.

causationEstimate.description: The same quantity estimated FROM DATA: the bounds and point of ``causationQuantity`` plus the interval around them. lower/upper is the identified set — assumption-free Tian-Pearl bounds, the same width at any sample size. The pair of ci keys is one pair of names for two different objects, and ``ci_width_is`` is which one this row holds; it used to be recovered from whether ``point`` was null, separately, by every surface that needed it.

ci_width_is.description: Which of the two objects the ci pair holds on THIS run: 'sampling' when monotonicity bought a point and the pair is that point's bootstrap interval, 'outer_band' when it did not and the pair is a conservative band on [lower, upper]. Written by the estimator, which is the only thing that saw which came out. Null exactly when no interval was resampled at all, and then there is no width to be about anything. Vocabulary: themis.intervals.Width, where each member also carries what would narrow it — which is the half that decides what a reader does next and the half a bare pair of numbers cannot carry.

gformulaFactorStats.description: The per-stratum sufficient statistics one g-formula ATE was summed from: conditional_strata (one {z, arm, n, y_sum} per contributing (arm, z) cell, so E[Y|arm,z] = y_sum/n) and the covariate marginal as marginal_counts ({z, count} per z) + marginal_total (P(z) = count/total). z is the adjustment-value key (empty array in the no-adjustment case).

componentEstimate.description: A decomposition component: point estimate + bootstrap percentile CI (used by the four-way decomposition).

cdeReferenceEstimate.description: CDE-for-a-set at one reference level: the mediator level the whole block is held fixed at (0 = all at control, 1 = all at treated), the point CDE, and its bootstrap percentile CI.

ratioComponentEstimate.description: A ratio-scale four-way component: point + percentile CI whose bounds may be null (no bootstrap requested, or all resample draws non-finite).

precisionBudget.description: Iter 151+152: post-hoc precision budgeting per VISION 2026-04-26 §'输出 (2)'. Tells the user how much more N is needed to halve the current 95% CI. SE ∝ 1/√N → N_new = N_old · (W_old/W_new)². Helper: themis.output.sample_size.estimate_n_for_target_ci_half_width. Iter 160 added relative_width = half_width / |point| so the renderer's '>30% of point' surface heuristic is mechanical instead of LLM judgment; omitted when point is ~0.

name.description: Must match the name of an enclosing sum's bind.name.

valueExpr.description: A concrete literal value or a reference to a bound value variable introduced by an enclosing sum.

value.description: Concrete literal, varRef bound by enclosing sum, or absent (the value is bound externally by the enclosing query's context — e.g., identify query's target or given atoms).
