given.description: Valued atoms conditioned on. May be empty. Refers to any model-distribution conditional, not only literal Theta entries.

name.description: Fresh value-variable name introduced by the enclosing sum. Referenced by varRef in the body.

over.description: Atom whose value domain is iterated. Validator MUST enforce that this atom is ground (contains no var terms).

gap.description: What kind of shortfall this is, stated by the kernel that hit it. Orthogonal to 'kind', which says which channel repairs it. Restricted to the species a missing item can be (themis.types.MISSING_ITEM_GAPS) — the wider gapKind set also covers caveats read off the program, which no missing item raises.

observable.description: What measuring would settle this item, when measuring would. Present on the parameter asks the kernel builds from a probability key; absent when nothing observable repairs the item (no admissible adjustment set, an undeclared assumption). A consumer holding a sample decides from this whether that sample answers the ask, instead of parsing the rendered 'P(...)' in 'name'.

variables.description: Variable names, sorted, that the sample must measure.

population.description: The population the sample must be drawn from. Absent for the population under study — the one a supplied DataFrame is a sample of. When present it names a different population (a transport target, a second site), which the study sample does not settle however many of the variables it holds.

superseded_by_estimation.description: True when the estimation layer answering this query settles the ask, whatever it answers. Set on a precondition the identification layer imposes before it will write an estimand (declare monotonicity and the Wald ratio identifies the LATE) which the estimation layer does not consult: once it has produced a number or a refusal, the number discloses in the assumption ledger what it rested on and the refusal says what to do instead. Absent (false) for an ask that survives estimation.

slot_label.description: Identifies which slot this source contributed to. Shapes: 'parameter:P(Y=y|X=x, ...)' for conditional lookups, 'observation:X=value' for observed atoms.

source.description: Verbatim annotations.source of the statement that pinned this slot (e.g. 'PubMed:12345', 'user_report'). Absent when the contributing statement had no source field set.

is_weakest.description: True when this source's confidence equals the composite min — i.e. this source is (one of) the binding constraints on the overall result confidence.

parameterSkeleton.description: Paste-ready stub for a missing probability CPT entry. Emitted by the investigation_pusher as investigationItem.skeleton when the MissingKind is 'parameter'. Round-trippable into a kernel_ast probabilityStatement once the user fills the numeric value.

value.description: Null in the freshly-emitted skeleton; the user fills it in before merging back via apply_patch_and_run. Once set, must fall in [0, 1] (enforced by merge).

annotations.description: Free-form metadata carried through merge (e.g. {"source": "TODO"} on emission, {"source": "user_report"} after fill).

variablePatch.description: Paste-ready stub for framing a declared variable. Emitted by slice F1 (DEFINE_VARIABLE investigation) as investigationItem.skeleton. The user fills nulls in the 'fields' map; 'existing' is read-only context.

existing.description: Read-only snapshot of framing fields already set on the VariableDeclaration. Merge never writes back into this map.

fields.description: Per-field fill surface. Each legal key maps to the kind that A0/F1 reports as a gap. Value null means the user has not filled it yet; any non-null value is interpreted by merge per field semantics.

target.description: Structured identifier matching the originating MissingItem.name.

skeleton.description: Paste-ready statement stub. Exactly one of two shapes — a parameter skeleton (the user fills in 'value') or a variable_patch (the user fills the fields dict). No third shape is accepted; new skeleton kinds land as explicit additions here.

gap.description: Carried verbatim from the originating missingItem.gap. The framing channel has no missing item and declares ambiguous_variable_definition, whose gap is built from framing_notes rather than from this item.

superseded_by_estimation.description: Carried verbatim from the originating missingItem, and read here rather than there: a pass that answers the query drops missing_information wholesale, so this is the surface on which a superseded ask can still be recognised and withdrawn.

boundsResult.description: Phase 12: symbolic bounds attached when point identification fails. Expressions are over observable distributions. When data is supplied via themis.estimate, the numeric end (estimation/bounds_numeric.py) additionally fills lower_value / upper_value / CI — the actual interval the data alone supports, computed by the SAME method named here. 'estimand' is required, symbolic or numeric: an interval whose quantity is left to be inferred from the method's reputation is not an answer, and this block once shipped an average-causal-effect interval under a question that asked for a single arm.

lower_expression.description: Symbolic expression for the lower bound, e.g. 'max(0, P(Y=1|X=1) - P(X=0))'.

assumptions.description: Method-specific assumptions (Manski natural: empty; Balke-Pearl: IV1/IV2/IV3).

data_required.description: Observable distributions a client must supply to evaluate the expressions.

width_when_uninformative.description: True when bounds collapse to the trivial range (e.g. [-1, 1] for risk difference) — answer is honest but not useful.

tightness.description: Whether a narrower set is consistent with the same assumptions. 'sharp' says this is the identified set itself and no better procedure reaches inside it; 'outer' says the interval is valid and possibly wider than the identified set, so there is room to tighten it WITHOUT any further assumption — a different offer from the one a wide sharp interval makes, and one a reader would otherwise have to infer from the method's reputation. Asked per bracketed quantity rather than per method: Manski-Tamer bounds the arm sharply and can report no contrast at all, because MTR ties the arms at the unit level. Vocabulary: themis.intervals.Tightness.

estimand.description: Which quantity lower_value / upper_value bracket. Every method here brackets the same one: the single interventional arm P(Y=y|do(X=x)) the query named. It is a one-member enum on purpose — not a formality, but the record that the domain collapsed: Balke-Pearl used to answer 'ace' here, which is a different question from the one an effect query asks and is undefined for a multi-valued treatment (no baseline arm) or outcome (not a probability difference). Where the ACE is defined it now travels in 'contrast', with its own endpoints. A second member belongs here only when a method brackets something a reader must tell apart from an arm.

contrast.description: Numeric end: a SECOND interval, over a second quantity, from the same identified set — the average causal effect, the queried arm against the other one. This is the quantity an 'effect' query actually asked for; the row's own estimand is one arm, which is a narrower question than the one that was put. Absent for a multi-valued treatment, where the difference has no baseline arm to be against. How it is obtained differs by method and the difference is load-bearing: Balke-Pearl runs its own pair of optimisations over the response-type polytope rather than doing arithmetic on lower_value/upper_value, because a difference of two quantities is contained in the difference of their intervals but is not in general equal to it when a model constrains the two arms together (on the binary IV model the two coincide on every table tried). Manski natural assumes nothing, so the arms' unobserved masses are disjoint sub-populations under no joint constraint and the difference of the intervals IS sharp — its width is then exactly 1 on every dataset, a fact about the assumptions rather than about the sample. Manski-Tamer reports none: MTR ties the arms together, so subtraction gives a valid but unsharp interval and nothing here says which a row is.

reference_value.description: The treatment level the queried arm is contrasted against.

tightness.description: The same question about THIS interval. A contrast can be an outer bound where the arm it was built from is sharp, which is why the row cannot answer for both with one word.

lower_value.description: Numeric end: data-evaluated lower bound. ABSENT when the symbolic bounds were not numerically evaluated (no data / refusal) — the producer omits the whole numeric end rather than nulling it, and this said null until someone read the producer. It is also the anchor of the numeric end: dependentRequired ties it to ci_lower / ci_upper, so a missing ci means 'not evaluated' when this is missing too and 'evaluated, no interval' when it is here.

numeric_uninformative.description: Numeric end: True when the evaluated interval spans (essentially) the whole logically-possible range (arm ∈ [0,1] → width≈1; ACE ∈ [−1,1] → width≈2) — honest but uninformative.

ci_lower.description: Numeric end: lower edge of the percentile-bootstrap OUTER band for the identified set (lower-α/2 quantile of the bootstrapped lower endpoint). Covers the identified interval with prob ≥ 1−ci_level; NOT an Imbens-Manski point CI.

ci_upper.description: Numeric end: upper edge of the outer band (upper-α/2 quantile of the bootstrapped upper endpoint).

ci_level.description: Numeric end: two-sided confidence level of the outer band.

sample_size.description: Numeric end: rows used to evaluate the bounds.

numeric_data_hash.description: Numeric end: SHA-256 of the data the numeric bounds were computed on (verifier reproducibility fingerprint).

numeric_data_columns.description: Numeric end: the columns ``numeric_data_hash`` was taken over, in the order it walked them — the denominator of that fingerprint. Normally NARROWER than numeric_estimate.data_columns on the same result — a Manski bound needs the exposure and the outcome where the estimator whose point it brackets also needed the adjustment set — so the two digests on one result differ because they are digests of different column sets, not because the data differed. Without each digest's own list that difference is unreadable, which is the whole of why this field exists.

instrument.description: The instrument this bound is taken around: present for the methods that use one (Balke-Pearl) and absent for the rest. ONE field because it is one fact — the symbolic producer writes the variable its response-function polytope is fitted around, the numeric end writes the column it read, and a row carrying both carries them equal. Describing it as the numeric end's is what let a second declaration of the same key be added under the symbolic end's name, which JSON resolves silently by keeping the last. It is also named inside lower_expression and notes, because a reader is shown sentences; but a sentence is a rendering, and the audit that had to confirm WHICH variable the polytope was fitted around used to recover it by running a regular expression over that sentence, which made the audit a check on the wording. Here it is read. Any finite cardinality — the response-function model enumerates a z→x map, and needs the instrument to have levels, not two of them.

numeric_cluster.description: Numeric end: cluster-id column when the CI used a pairs cluster bootstrap; absent for the i.i.d. bootstrap.

sufficient_statistics.description: Numeric end: recorded sufficient statistics that let the verifier RE-DERIVE [lower_value, upper_value] independently, rather than only metadata-auditing it. Balke-Pearl records the empirical P(X=x, Y=y | Z=z) table under 'P_xyz', the three level lists that say what its axes are, and the two indices naming which arm was asked about; the verifier re-runs the response-function LP over them. The level lists are not decoration: a |Z|x|X|x|Y| table is only interpretable if the producer says which axis is which, and a 2x3x2 table read as 3x2x2 re-derives a different interval and calls an honest producer a liar. Manski natural records the arm counts 'n' / 'n_joint_target_arm' / 'n_other_arm'; the verifier re-derives lower = n_joint/n and upper = (n_joint+n_other)/n (this matters for a MULTI-VALUED treatment, whose off-arm mass P(X≠x) pools several levels — a metadata-only audit cannot distinguish an honest complement from a fabricated one), plus 'n_joint_other_arm', which is what makes the 'contrast' interval re-derivable too — and the contrast is the quantity the query asked for, so leaving it unrecomputable would leave the least supervised number in the block sitting where the reader looks first. Absent for Manski-Tamer, whose one-sided tightening is anchored by the width/range invariants.

P_xyz.description: Balke-Pearl: empirical P(X=x, Y=y | Z=z) as a |Z|x|X|x|Y| nested array [z][x][y], indexed by sorted level positions.

treatment_levels.description: Balke-Pearl: the sorted treatment levels the P_xyz x-axis is indexed by.

outcome_levels.description: Balke-Pearl: the sorted outcome levels the P_xyz y-axis is indexed by.

instrument_levels.description: Balke-Pearl: the sorted instrument levels the P_xyz z-axis is indexed by.

arm_treatment_index.description: Balke-Pearl: position in treatment_levels of the intervened level — which arm the interval is about.

arm_outcome_index.description: Balke-Pearl: position in outcome_levels of the target level.

n.description: Manski natural: total rows the arm bound was computed on (= sample_size).

n_joint_target_arm.description: Manski natural: count of rows with X=x AND Y=y (the observed same-arm joint mass); lower_value = n_joint_target_arm / n.

n_other_arm.description: Manski natural: count of rows with X≠x (the pooled off-arm mass); width = n_other_arm / n.

n_joint_other_arm.description: Manski natural: count of rows with X≠x AND Y=y. Recorded unconditionally — it is a fact about the data, where having a baseline arm to contrast against is a fact about the treatment's cardinality — and it is the count the 'contrast' interval is re-derived from: lower = (n_joint_target_arm − n_joint_other_arm − (n − n_other_arm)) / n, upper = (n_joint_target_arm − n_joint_other_arm + n_other_arm) / n.

dataGapReport.description: Phase 10: top-level structured report on what data / assumptions / structural changes are still needed to make progress on the query. Gaps are sorted by severity (blocking > important > informational), then by derivation order within the same severity tier.

summary.description: One-line natural-language summary of the most blocking gap, or empty string when gaps is empty.

actionable_next_steps.description: User-facing suggestions in order of impact. Each entry is a complete sentence in Chinese; rendering layer reads these as-is.

answer_tier.description: The strongest answer available for a query whose question names an estimand, stated explicitly so consumers do not infer it from gap-severity ordering. Orthogonal to gap severity: an unidentifiable effect with informative IV / Manski bounds has a blocking gap yet answer_tier='interval'. point = point estimand identified (possibly pending θ); interval = point ID blocked but informative bounds available; none = neither (needs an assumption / stronger data). Absent only for cause / assoc, which ask about the graph and name no quantity.

dataGap.description: A single data / assumption / structural shortfall blocking some downstream output. Each gap maps to one or more upstream signals (derivation step, investigation_request, framing_note, verifier check) carried in provenance.

kind.description: Categorical gap kind. Enum extends as new boards (measurement error, g-methods, L3b nested counterfactuals) come online.

signature.description: Sub-classification within the kind. For missing_distribution: 'marginal' | 'conditional' | 'joint'. Omitted for kinds with no sub-shape.

severity.description: blocking = downstream output cannot be produced at all; important = output produced but quality reduced (e.g. needs untestable assumption, only bounds available); informational = caveat / framing note only.

description.description: Free-form explanation of the gap. Renderer translates to user-facing copy via response_rendering templates.

required_data.description: Optional. What kind of data, on which population, on which variables, would close this gap. Generator fills what it can infer; missing fields stay absent.

sampling_point_count.description: Phase 13: distinct X values to sample for dose-response curve fitting (≥4 recommended).

confounders_required.description: Phase 13: predicates the user must measure and adjust for (typically the backdoor set).

time_window.description: Phase 13: recommended measurement schedule for dose-response data collection.

sutva_concerns.description: Phase 13: SUTVA / interference risks to control for in study design.

blocks.description: Which downstream output this gap prevents.

if_provided.description: What becomes possible if this gap is filled (e.g. 'point estimate with bootstrap CI').

alternative_paths.description: Alternative ways to make progress without this exact data (e.g. 'accept Balke-Pearl bounds' / 'add untestable monotonicity assumption').

provenance.description: One gap may be triggered by multiple upstream signals; array allows multi-source attribution. T10-1 verifier checks every ref resolves to a real artifact in the result envelope.

ref_id.description: Stable identifier within the chosen kind: derivation step_id, investigation_request.target, framing_note.predicate, or verifier rule name.

target.description: For a single-item request this is the MissingItem.name. For a grouped request, a short summary ('N items').

group.description: MissingKind.value for parameter/observation/sample/structure/assumption groups, or 'framing' for DEFINE_VARIABLE (slice F1) — items in the same request share a channel.

items.description: Per-item details within this grouped request. Always populated in v0.2 (length >= 1).
